name: Open-chest shirt styling

card.summary: Wearing a shirt with several top buttons undone to show the neck and upper chest, used to make the neck and torso look broader and the outfit more relaxed.
card.note: A style choice; how many buttons read as appropriate varies by setting.

quick.overview:
Open-chest styling means leaving the top buttons of a shirt undone so the collarbones and upper chest show. People use it to open up the neckline, show off neck and chest development and give an outfit a relaxed, confident look.

Fashion writing treats the number of open buttons as a formality signal: unbuttoning the top one is standard without a tie, while more is described as increasingly casual. No studies test the look's effect on attractiveness.
quick.how: Practitioners leave one to several top buttons open, often on camp, Cuban-collar, linen or casual button-up shirts, sometimes layered over a T-shirt. The look is typically paired with visible chest or neck development, jewelry or tailoring.
quick.risks: No health risk is attached. Reference sources note that unbuttoning two or more is considered overly casual in many US and UK business settings, so the look can clash with dress codes.

lead: Open-chest shirt styling is the practice of wearing a button-up shirt with more than the usual top button undone so that the neck, collarbones and upper chest are visible. People use it to draw attention to the neck and chest, to make the upper body look broader or more developed, and to signal a relaxed style.

Dress-shirt reference material describes the convention: with a tie, the top button is fastened, without one US and UK wearers almost never button it, and unbuttoning two or more is considered overly casual in those settings, while two undone is more common in France.[1] Some American men wear the top two buttons undone for casual office wear, leaving the fourth open is widely seen as too casual, and the most casual option is a fully open shirt over a T-shirt.[1]
No clinical studies examine the look. Related medical research on neckwear, for example, measured eye pressure under tight neckties versus an open collar.[2][3]

chain: Neck, collarbones and upper chest exposed

angle.text: The undone buttons change the neckline so that chest and neck development is visible. How far it is opened sets how formal or casual the outfit reads.

infobox: Button-up, camp or Cuban-collar, casual shirts
Casual; more open buttons read as more casual[1]

paras: Collar style is the main indicator of formality in a dress shirt.[1] Polo shirts are more likely to be worn with the top button fastened, and younger people have recently fastened the top button even without a tie.[1] A 2009 Seattle Times article covered the unbuttoning trend.[1]

No studies found. Studies of tight neckties found that a tight tie raised intraocular pressure compared with an open collar in normal subjects and glaucoma patients, and one examined extended wear.[2][3]
